titleText.es: Al tercer trimestre tendrás cientos de bebés dentro de ti.
titleText.en: By the third trimester, there will be hundreds of babies inside you.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive closely translates the official title text and preserves the same deliberately reckless extrapolation joke.

regions.labelEs: COMO PUEDES VER, A FINALES DEL PRÓXIMO MES TENDRÁS MÁS DE CINCUENTA MARIDOS. SERÁ MEJOR QUE INTENTES CONSEGUIR PRECIOS DE MAYORISTA PARA LOS PASTELES DE BODA.

applications.explanationEn: Como introduces the claimed visible conclusion, puedes changes for one familiar listener, and ver stays in its unchanged dictionary form after puedes.
A finales del introduces the period's late part, and próximo mes supplies the complete period being located in time.
Próximo uses its masculine singular ending -o to match the masculine singular noun mes.
Tener uses its irregular future stem tendr- and adds -ás for one familiar listener.
Más de marks a numerical threshold being exceeded, while cincuenta maridos supplies the full quantity.
Será places the evaluation in future time, mejor states what is preferable, que introduces the recommended action, and intentes is the changed recommendation form of intentar.
Ser keeps its full dictionary form and adds -á for a future statement about one person or thing.
Intentes changes to fit the recommendation, while conseguir follows directly in its unchanged dictionary form as the action to attempt.
Precios names the rates, de links them to their commercial category, and mayorista identifies the wholesale level.
Pasteles is plural for multiple cakes, and de boda identifies the event they are made for.

cards.noteEn: Hobby is an English loanword used in Spanish. A common Spanish alternative is afición or pasatiempo.

example.en: Photography is my hobby.

cards.answerEn: to extrapolate; to extend a trend beyond the known data
cards.noteEn: Extrapolar means using an observed pattern to estimate what lies outside the observations already available.

example.es: No conviene extrapolar una tendencia a partir de dos datos.
example.en: It is unwise to extrapolate a trend from two data points.

cards.promptEs: extrapolar · ayer · hoy · más de cincuenta maridos
cards.questionEn: Why is the graph's prediction absurd?
cards.answerEn: It draws a straight trend through only two observations—zero husbands yesterday and one today—and extends that line far beyond the observed time. Two points always determine a line, but they provide almost no evidence that the real situation will continue linearly.
cards.noteEn: The title text repeats the same error with pregnancy: it projects a rapidly growing count into a later trimester as though every short-term change must continue unchanged.

cards.questionEn: How can you introduce a conclusion that the other person can supposedly see from the evidence?
cards.answerEn: Use como puedes ver, meaning ‘as you can see.’
cards.noteEn: Como means ‘as,’ puedes means ‘you can,’ and ver stays in its unchanged dictionary form after puedes. The phrase often introduces an explanation or claimed conclusion.

example.es: Como puedes ver, la puerta está abierta.
example.en: As you can see, the door is open.

cards.answerEn: you can; you are able to
no separate English word; begins a finales de, “in the late part of”
cards.noteEn: The preposition a is required in the time expression a finales de. Natural English normally renders the full expression with “in,” not by translating a alone.

example.en: They arrived in late June.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something happens in the late part of a month, year, decade, or other period?
cards.answerEn: Use a finales de, followed by the period.
cards.noteEn: A is fixed in this expression, finales is the plural of final, “end,” and de introduces the period. English commonly says “in late…” or “at the end of…,” depending on context.

example.es: El curso termina a finales de julio.
example.en: The course ends in late July.

cards.answerEn: late part; end (in a finales de)
cards.noteEn: Final means “end.” Its plural form finales is used in a finales de to locate something near the end of a month, year, decade, or other period.

example.es: La tienda abrió a finales de verano.
example.en: The store opened in late summer.

cards.answerEn: of the; introduces the period after a finales
cards.noteEn: Del combines de and el. In a finales del mes, it connects a finales to the masculine period mes; natural English usually renders the complete expression as ‘late in the month’ or ‘at the end of the month.’

example.en: We will return late in the summer.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.noteEn: Tendrás is the future form of tener for one familiar person. Tener changes its future stem to tendr- before the ending -ás.

example.en: Tomorrow you will have more time.

cards.questionEn: How do you say what someone will do in Spanish?
cards.answerEn: Keep the action verb in its dictionary form and add a future ending such as -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, or -án.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. The ending identifies the person: sentir plus -á gives sentirá, and ver plus -á gives verá. A few common verbs change their stem, but use the same endings.

example.en: Marta will call tomorrow.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that an amount is more than a particular number or quantity?
cards.answerEn: Put más de directly before the number or amount.
cards.noteEn: Use más de when the next element is a quantity being exceeded. Use más que instead when directly comparing people, things, qualities, or actions: más de diez libros, but Ana lee más que Luis.

example.en: She bought more than three books.

cards.noteEn: Before a number or other quantity, Spanish uses más de for “more than.” This de is different from más que, which commonly compares one person, thing, or action with another.

example.en: There are more than twenty people.

cards.noteEn: Será is the future form of ser for one person or thing.

example.en: Tomorrow will be another day.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that it is or will be better for someone to do something?
cards.answerEn: Use the needed form of ser, then mejor que, and change the following action verb to the form used for a recommendation.
cards.noteEn: The form of ser can show the time: es mejor que, será mejor que, or sería mejor que. Because the following action is being judged preferable rather than reported as a fact, its verb takes a special subjunctive form such as llegues, salgamos, or intenten.

example.en: It is better for you to arrive early.

cards.noteEn: Mejor compares one option with another. It does not change for gender: una solución mejor and un plan mejor both use mejor.

example.en: We need a better idea.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an evaluation with the recommended action
cards.noteEn: After es, será, or sería mejor, que introduces the action judged preferable. Spanish then uses a specially changed verb form for that recommendation.

example.en: It will be better for us to leave early.

cards.answerEn: you try; you attempt (special form after a recommendation)
cards.noteEn: Intentes is a changed form of intentar for one familiar person. It appears here because the action is recommended after será mejor que rather than stated as a fact.

example.en: It is better for you to try to rest.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone tries to do an action?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of intentar followed directly by the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: No linking preposition is needed between the two verbs. Intento abrir means “I try to open,” and intentamos salir means “we try to leave.” The attempted action stays in its basic -ar, -er, or -ir form.

example.en: We try to open the window.

cards.answerEn: to obtain; to work out; to achieve
cards.noteEn: Conseguir can mean obtaining a result through effort, not only physically getting an object.

example.en: We want to reach an agreement.

cards.questionEn: How do you refer to a wholesale price rather than a retail price?
cards.answerEn: Use precio de mayorista, or precios de mayorista in the plural.
cards.noteEn: De links precio to mayorista, the wholesale level or seller category. The first noun changes for number, while mayorista keeps the same written form here.

example.es: La empresa ofrece precios de mayorista.
example.en: The company offers wholesale prices.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an item to its type
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between an item and the noun that identifies its type. English often puts the type noun first instead: libro de historia becomes “history book.”

example.en: I bought a history book.

cards.noteEn: A mayorista sells large quantities to businesses rather than individual retail customers. After de in precios de mayorista, it describes wholesale-level prices.

example.es: La tienda compra la fruta a un mayorista.
example.en: The shop buys the fruit from a wholesaler.

cards.answerEn: for; introduces the product that a price or rate applies to
cards.noteEn: After a word such as precio or tarifa, para can introduce the item or service whose price is being discussed.

example.es: Pedimos una tarifa para el servicio completo.
example.en: We asked for a rate for the complete service.

cards.answerEn: Say pastel de boda; use pasteles de boda for more than one.
cards.noteEn: De connects pastel to the kind of event it is made for. Spanish does not turn boda into an adjective.

example.es: Encargaron un pastel de boda pequeño.
example.en: They ordered a small wedding cake.
